claim: QA round 24 (2026-11-07): a sender address is never a LIKE pattern. The gateway bridge and both prospects.service provider lookups pass the address through inbound-headers.ts likeExactly (escapes backslash, %, _ and *); EmailParsingAgent._find_provider_by_email and both EmailIntelAgent sender lookups pass it through email_parsing_agent.like_exactly. ilike is kept, escaped, because providers.contact_email keeps the typed case and is unique on lower(contact_email), so eq on the folded address would miss Sales@BigDist.com. Both parsers refuse % and * in the domain, so From %@% names nobody. Proof: inbound-headers.spec.ts 'a sender is matched exactly' and test_email_sender_attribution.py round-24 tests, both over an ILIKE-emulating store with two houses.
verify: grep -qF '.ilike("contact_email", likeExactly(senderEmail))' apps/api-gateway/src/common/orchestrator/rabbitmq-bridge.service.ts && ! grep -qE '\.ilike\("contact_email", (senderEmail|p\.sender_email)' apps/api-gateway/src/common/orchestrator/rabbitmq-bridge.service.ts apps/api-gateway/src/common/orchestrator/prospects.service.ts && [ "$(grep -cF 'likeExactly(p.sender_email' apps/api-gateway/src/common/orchestrator/prospects.service.ts)" = 2 ] && grep -qF '.ilike("contact_email", like_exactly(normalized))' services/agent-orchestrator/agents/email_parsing_agent.py && [ "$(grep -cF '.ilike("email", like_exactly(sender_email' services/agent-orchestrator/agents/email_intel_agent.py)" = 2 ] && grep -qF '@[^\s@<>()",;%*]+$/' apps/api-gateway/src/communications/inbound-headers.ts && grep -qF '@[^\s@<>()",;%*]+$' services/agent-orchestrator/agents/email_parsing_agent.py && grep -qF 'return address.replace(/[\\%_*]/g' apps/api-gateway/src/communications/inbound-headers.ts
